items.label: Industry: Beauty & Personal Care Retail
items.detail: Selected via account-grounded holdings: the IBKR connector was authenticated this session, and the account directly holds ULTA (Ulta Beauty, 30 sh, $16,310.70 market value, Trading Sleeve, bought off a 2026-09-21 Momentum HIGH call at $552.81). US beauty & personal care market estimates for 2026 range $580-694B across research firms (wide dispersion reflects differing scope definitions), growing to roughly $742B by 2030 (~6.3% CAGR), with brick-and-mortar cosmetics/personal-care stores specifically projected to reach $509B by 2030 (~7.5% CAGR). 2026 is a genuine inflection year for the specialty-retail channel: Sephora's rollout to essentially all ~1,100 Kohl's stores is complete, TikTok Shop has become the 4th-largest US health/beauty e-commerce retailer, Amazon is pushing a Premium Beauty storefront, and Ulta itself just lost its 600+ store Target shop-in-shop channel (non-renewal effective August 2026) -- all while Ulta's core loyalty-driven business keeps beating guidance. Not covered by any prior scout cycle (critical minerals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13, nuclear/SMR 2026-09-20, neoclouds 2026-09-27).

items.label: ULTA
items.detail: Ulta Beauty -- held, 30 sh, $16,310.70 market value (-$160.30 unrealized, Trading Sleeve, called by Momentum on 2026-09-21 at $552.81). Reinforcing evidence this cycle: Q2 FY2026 beat (net sales +8.9% to $3.036B vs. $2.973B consensus; comp sales +3.8%; EPS $6.55, +13.3% YoY) and FY2026 guidance raised twice this year -- now 6.7-7.2% net sales growth (from 6-7%), 3.2-3.7% comp growth (from 2.5-3.5%), EPS $28.70-$29.00 (from $28.36-$28.80). The loyalty program -- 95% of sales -- grew to ~47M members (+4% YoY), the core moat still intact. Real risk, not glossed over: the Ulta-at-Target shop-in-shop (600+ stores) will not renew past August 2026, and Sephora's completed rollout to essentially all ~1,100 Kohl's stores (prestige brands like MAC and Charlotte Tilbury now in 850+ locations) is explicitly using Kohl's suburban footprint to contest Ulta's traditional geography; management's own second-half guidance (4-5% sales growth vs. first-half pace) already prices in some deceleration. Hold-through-it, not a blind add.

items.label: ELF
items.detail: e.l.f. Beauty -- not held. The clearest growth re-acceleration story in the group: FY2026 net sales growth guidance raised to 22-23%, powered by the ~$1B Rhode (Hailey Bieber) acquisition closed August 2025 -- Rhode is tracking to $500M+ in annualized global retail sales and contributed $128M to Q3 net-sales growth alone. Stock last $104.50 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-04), down ~29% from its 52-week high of $147.75 despite the accelerating fundamentals -- the market appears to be discounting mass-beauty's heaviest China-sourcing exposure in this set (multiple trade-press reports flag Chinese cosmetics-component duties as high as 54%) and post-acquisition integration/multiple-compression risk rather than the growth number itself.
items.diversification_note: No current beauty-sector holding other than ULTA, which is a retailer rather than a brand; ELF adds exposure to the mass-beauty manufacturing/brand side of the same industry, diversifying the thesis beyond retail-channel execution risk.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; size down relative to a full-conviction bet given the name's outsized China-sourcing/tariff exposure relative to peers in this set.

items.label: EL
items.detail: Estee Lauder Companies -- not held. A genuine turnaround rather than a pure value trap: fourth consecutive quarter of sales growth, Q1 FY2026 organic net sales +3% to $3.45B (beat consensus), China net sales +9%, and travel retail improving on stronger Asia/Hainan duty-free trends. The Profit Recovery and Growth Plan targets ~$1.2B in annual gross benefits, and new CEO Stephane de La Faverie's 'Beauty Reimagined' strategy is explicitly expanding distribution into Amazon, TikTok Shop, and Sephora -- the same disruptive channels flagged as risks elsewhere in this report, here working in an incumbent's favor. Stock last $91.97 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-04), still ~24% off its 52-week high of $120.75, reflecting real unresolved risk: this is a multi-year restructuring with genuine execution risk, and the prior multi-year decline (China weakness, travel-retail collapse, dividend cuts) is recent enough that one good quarter is not full proof of a durable inflection.
items.diversification_note: Prestige/luxury beauty manufacturer exposure, distinct from ULTA's specialty-retail-channel risk and ELF's mass-market/tariff risk -- a different risk profile within the same industry thesis.
items.suggested_size: Starter position given this is an early-stage, unproven turnaround rather than a confirmed inflection.

items.label: IPAR
items.detail: Interparfums -- not held. The cleanest licensing-moat business in the industry: a portfolio of long-duration fragrance licenses that keep renewing rather than churning -- Guess extended 23 years to 2048, Roberto Cavalli/Just Cavalli extended 20 years to 2046, a new Puma license through 2037, and new David Beckham and Nautica licenses added in 2026 -- demonstrating major fashion houses prefer Interparfums over building fragrance capability in-house. Stock last $114.00 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-04). Not a 'New idea' to act on now: company guidance explicitly frames 2026 as a 'bridge year' -- flat sales (~$1.48B) and lower EPS (~$4.85) -- because the Puma and Longchamp launches don't land until 2027. Worth tracking into early 2027 for the first read on whether the new-license pipeline actually reaccelerates growth, rather than buying into the flat year.

items.label: Social commerce (TikTok Shop) disintermediating specialty/prestige retail
items.detail: No specific ticker -- a structural channel-shift risk sitting under every name in this report, ULTA most directly. TikTok Shop is now the 4th-largest health & beauty e-commerce retailer in the US (sales above $4.4B, beauty = 22.5% of platform GMV, category dollar sales +107.7% YoY in the 52 weeks to December 2025) and converts in-app checkout at 5-8% versus 1.5-2% for Sephora.com -- a structurally better funnel built on creator credibility rather than store or loyalty-card relationships. This competes directly with the loyalty-card model (Ulta's 47M-member program, 95% of sales) that is ULTA's core moat, while Estee Lauder and (via Sephora) LVMH are leaning into the channel rather than resisting it. Track TikTok Shop's beauty GMV growth and Ulta's loyalty-member engagement each quarter as the real test of whether specialty retail's role is shrinking or merely shifting channels.

items.label: MoCRA compliance burden & China tariffs accelerating indie-brand consolidation
items.detail: No specific ticker -- a regulatory/trade theme shaping the industry's next wave of structure. MoCRA (the 2022 federal cosmetics-safety law) adds real compliance cost this cycle -- 2026 is a facility-registration renewal year for brands that first registered in 2024, with mandatory 15-business-day adverse-event reporting now in force -- while FDA has already missed its own deadlines on GMP rules and fragrance-allergen labeling (both pushed to 2027 or later), so the compliance bar is rising gradually rather than all at once. Separately, China-sourced tariffs (up to 54% on some cosmetics components, though select categories like cosmetics-application brushes saw relief in an early-October 2026 US-China deal) raise fixed costs disproportionately for small indie brands without scale. Both pressures favor further consolidation: BeautyMatter tracked 83 M&A deals in Q1 2026 alone (+40.7% YoY), with L'Oreal (Creed, Color Wow), Estee Lauder (Forest Essentials), and PE buyers (Advent/Salt & Stone) all actively rolling up founder-led brands. This is a tailwind for EL and ELF specifically as acquirers with balance-sheet scale, and a watch item for any future scout cycle that surfaces a standalone indie-brand acquisition target before it gets bought.
